newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 16 to 966 in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 16 to 966 in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 966 as of June 20, down 16 from the prior week and 193 above the year-ago total of 773, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by eight to 824, while rigs working offshore fell nine to 117. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose one to 25.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in California, which was down by five. Oklahoma was down by five and Texas was up by six.
The Gulf of Mexico rig count fell nine to 117.

A total of 347 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down 46 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas fell by 15 to 570, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects dipped by one to three.
There were 202 rigs drilling directionally, 70 drilling horizontally and 694 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 41 to 347, versus 269 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
